lead: >-
  Tours of Brazil differ in the regions they combine: a short trip to Rio and Iguazu, wildlife watching in the Pantanal, a journey into the Amazon, beaches in the northeast, and a major itinerary across several natural regions all require different amounts of time and preparation. Compare our current programs by transfers, duration, travel format, and included services.
---

## Which tour of Brazil should you choose?

**Start with the experience that matters most to you and the number of days you have.** [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and [Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) can be combined in a relatively short trip. The [Pantanal](/brazil/place/pantanal/), [Bonito](/brazil/place/bonito/), the [Amazon](/brazil/place/manaus-amazon/), and [Lençóis Maranhenses](/brazil/place/lencois-maranhenses/), however, are far apart. The more of these regions a tour includes, the more carefully you should review its flights, transfers, and nights in each place.

Our catalog includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Brazil as a main destination. Options range from short sightseeing itineraries and private journeys to group tours, themed trips, and programs that also visit neighboring countries. Here you can **compare specific tours**; our [guide to Brazil](/brazil/) explores its geography, regions, and seasons in more depth.

| Main goal | Itinerary to compare |
|---|---|
| Rio and waterfalls | [Rio and Iguazu in 7 days](/brazil/tour/brazil-rio-iguazu-private-tour/) |
| Wildlife and beach | [Rio, Iguazu, Pantanal, Búzios](/brazil/tour/brazil-rio-foz-do-iguacu-pantanal-buzios-12-days/) |
| Pantanal, Bonito, dunes | [Three regions in 8 days](/brazil/tour/pantanal-bonito-lencois-maranhenses-8-days/) |
| Extended nature journey | [Grand Brazil Adventure, 17 days](/brazil/tour/grand-brazil-adventure-17-days/) |
| Northeast coast and ocean | [Recife and Fernando de Noronha](/brazil/tour/northeast-brazil-recife-porto-de-galinhas-fernando-de-noronha-10-days/) |
| Southern states | [Gramado, canyons, Florianópolis](/brazil/tour/southern-brazil-rio-iguazu-gramado-florianopolis-12-days/) |

Each option has its strengths. The number of attractions in a tour title does not tell you how intensive the itinerary will be: time spent at each place and the arrangements for getting between them are often more important.

## Your first trip: Rio de Janeiro, Iguazu and the ocean

The [7-day private “Rio and Iguazu” tour](/brazil/tour/brazil-rio-iguazu-private-tour/) focuses on two major stops. In Rio, visitors can see Sugarloaf Mountain, Corcovado with its Christ statue, and historic neighborhoods. Near Iguazu, the waterfalls and national park trails take center stage. This combination suits travelers visiting Brazil for the first time who want varied experiences without crossing the entire continent.

With a few additional days, compare it with the [12-day Rio–Iguazu–Pantanal–Búzios itinerary](/brazil/tour/brazil-rio-foz-do-iguacu-pantanal-buzios-12-days/). It adds wildlife watching in the Pantanal and a beach finale in [Búzios](/brazil/place/buzios/). The journey becomes more varied, but there are more transport legs and changes of accommodation.

Iguazu has one detail that affects the choice of itinerary. [Foz do Iguaçu in Brazil](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and [Puerto Iguazú in Argentina](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) lie on opposite sides of the border. Brazilian routes are famous for their panoramic views of the falls; the Argentine side has a network of walkways close to the cascades. **Having Iguazu in the tour title does not itself confirm visits to both national parks.** Check the daily itinerary, included tickets, and any border crossing.

## Nature-focused tours: Pantanal, Bonito and the Amazon compared

### Pantanal: watching animals in floodplain landscapes

The [Pantanal](/brazil/place/pantanal/) attracts visitors with birds, capybaras, caimans, and other wildlife. Where you stay, the timing of excursions, transport, and seasonal water levels are particularly important. A boat-based photographic safari has different conditions from watching wildlife along roads and trails.

If the Pantanal is your main goal, compare the number of **full days spent observing wildlife**, not just the total nights in the country. On the [grand 17-day journey](/brazil/tour/grand-brazil-adventure-17-days/), it forms one part of a longer route. [Tours through the Pantanal](/brazil/place/pantanal/tour/) may place a different emphasis on the region. A list of possible animals is not a guarantee that every species will be seen.

### Bonito: clear rivers, caves and water activities

[Bonito](/brazil/place/bonito/) offers a different kind of nature experience. Travelers come for transparent rivers, karst formations, and water-based excursions. The activities depend on the program: observing underwater life, walking through a cave, and scuba diving require different preparation and conditions.

The [8-day Pantanal, Bonito and Lençóis Maranhenses tour](/brazil/tour/pantanal-bonito-lencois-maranhenses-8-days/) connects three distant natural regions. It is a busy itinerary, so the sequence of transfers deserves particular attention. If you want several consecutive days of relaxed wildlife watching, spend longer in the Pantanal. If you prefer different kinds of natural attractions, the combined trip offers greater contrasts.

### Amazon: a lodge or a river journey

In the [Amazon](/brazil/place/manaus-amazon/), the experience depends heavily on accommodation and river routes. One program may be based at a lodge with excursions into the forest, another on overnight stays aboard a boat traveling between river sections. Even tours of equal duration vary in the amount of time spent on the water and in the jungle.

For example, the [3-day VIP program around Manaus and Anavilhanas](/brazil/tour/amazon-manaus-anavilhanas-vip-3-days/) features a seaplane flight, accommodation at Mirante do Gavião Amazon Lodge, and specific nature activities included in the itinerary. It is a particular short travel product, not a standard set of services for every [Amazon tour](/brazil/place/manaus-amazon/tour/).

When comparing Amazon itineraries, check where the lodge is, how river transfers work, whether there are evening excursions, and how many activities are genuinely included. Water levels also matter: they affect access to certain places and the way visitors experience the forest.

## Lençóis Maranhenses: when the lagoons are your main goal

[Lençóis Maranhenses](/brazil/place/lencois-maranhenses/) is a landscape of dunes and freshwater lagoons. The lagoons fill with seasonal rainfall, so photographs of full blue pools do not guarantee the same view at every time of year.

The [17-day Brazil itinerary](/brazil/tour/grand-brazil-adventure-17-days/) combines Lençóis with Rio, Iguazu, the Pantanal, and Bonito. It suits travelers who want to experience several different natural regions on one journey. If your priority is dunes and lagoons, compare [tours visiting Lençóis](/brazil/place/lencois-maranhenses/tour/). Pay particular attention to the season, connections from São Luís, and the time actually reserved for walking among the dunes.

## Beach tours: the Rio coast or the northeast

Beach holidays in Brazil also take different forms. You can add [Búzios](/brazil/place/buzios/) or [Paraty](/brazil/place/paraty/) to a stay in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). This combines a major city with smaller coastal communities, walks, and time by the ocean.

The [10-day “Recife, Porto de Galinhas and Fernando de Noronha” tour](/brazil/tour/northeast-brazil-recife-porto-de-galinhas-fernando-de-noronha-10-days/) covers a different region. It features Recife, Olinda, the northeast coast, and an island stage. Compare it with the classic Rio–Iguazu combination according to your goal: here, the ocean and northeast are more central than major waterfalls or a long sequence of inland destinations.

For islands and protected natural areas, check actual flights, access restrictions, and whether boat excursions and mandatory fees are included. If the sea is your main priority, begin with [Brazil beach-holiday tours](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/brazil/). To include wildlife, also compare [nature tours in Brazil](/interests/wildlife/tours/brazil/).

## Coffee, culture and events: specialized travel interests

A specific interest can matter more than a list of famous attractions. For example, the [8-day Brazil coffee tour](/brazil/tour/brazil-coffee-tour-8-days/) combines Rio and Iguazu with the history of Brazilian coffee. If your goal is to visit coffee farms and understand production, compare trips in the [Brazil coffee tours catalog](/interests/coffee-tours/tours/brazil/) rather than searching among all tours that serve breakfast.

Travelers interested in colonial architecture, traditions, and museums may prefer routes through [Salvador](/brazil/place/salvador/), [Ouro Preto](/brazil/place/ouro-preto/), and [Paraty](/brazil/place/paraty/). In [cultural and historical tours of Brazil](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/brazil/), these interests become a central reason for choosing the trip.

Carnival and other festival journeys depend on the calendar. Check the exact event and tour date first, then choose any nature and beach additions. General options appear under [Events and Festivals](/interests/events-and-festivals/), but an event-related theme does not replace the list of activities included in the program.

Finally, compare [VIP tours in Brazil](/vip/brazil/) by their actual contents: accommodation, transfers, guiding, and whether excursions are private. The category name alone does not establish that a private plane, yacht, or particular class of hotel is included.

## How many days should you spend in Brazil?

| Duration | What you can plan |
|---|---|
| 3–5 days | One city or region |
| 6–9 days | Two main stops |
| 10–13 days | Several regions |
| 14–17+ days | An extended journey |

These are guidelines, not rigid categories for the current catalog. [Three days in the Amazon](/brazil/tour/amazon-manaus-anavilhanas-vip-3-days/) is a short standalone program. The [8-day Pantanal, Bonito and Lençóis itinerary](/brazil/tour/pantanal-bonito-lencois-maranhenses-8-days/) covers several remote regions and requires tighter logistics.

Count not just days, but also **nights in each location**. A morning flight followed by several hours of ground transfer can consume most of a day. This matters particularly on long routes from the Amazon to northeastern states or across southern Brazil. Weather-dependent nature excursions benefit from spare time when the total length of the journey allows for it.

## Price and format: what to compare besides the amount

A tour price is meaningful only together with the basis on which it is quoted: per traveler, for a particular type of room, for a private party, or as part of a group program. Compare the same currency, number of travelers, nights, meals, flights, entrance tickets, and excursions. One tour may include domestic flights while another lists them as separate expenses.

The word “private” describes the format of the trip as a whole. Individual cruises, outings, or nature excursions within it can sometimes be organized for a group of visitors. Check the conditions and inclusions of the actual product rather than drawing conclusions from a single word in the title.

One more consideration: Brazil is a vast country with different climatic patterns. For [Lençóis Maranhenses](/brazil/place/lencois-maranhenses/), the season when lagoons fill matters; for the [Pantanal](/brazil/place/pantanal/), water levels affect wildlife watching; for the Amazon, rivers follow seasonal cycles. Decide on your most important destination first, select a suitable period for it, and then consider the other regions.

If you plan to visit the Argentine side of Iguazu or continue to [Argentina](/argentina/), check visa and document requirements for your nationality and actual route. You can compare combinations of neighboring countries under [multi-country tours](/multi-country/).

## Frequently asked questions about choosing a Brazil tour

### Which itinerary is good for a first visit?

[Rio and Iguazu in 7 days](/brazil/tour/brazil-rio-iguazu-private-tour/) is a straightforward introduction: city, ocean, and waterfalls. For wildlife or additional beach time, choose a longer journey featuring the Pantanal or the coast. Take extra flights and the number of nights into account.

### Can I see the Pantanal, Bonito and Lençóis in eight days?

There is an [8-day itinerary](/brazil/tour/pantanal-bonito-lencois-maranhenses-8-days/) covering all three. Because the regions are far apart, some of the time is spent traveling. For a more relaxed experience in one region, allow additional days.

### How does the Amazon differ from the Pantanal for nature watching?

Tropical forest and river routes are central to the Amazon experience. The Pantanal is known for open floodplains and animal watching on land and water. Wildlife visibility, seasonal conditions, and accommodation differ, so choose according to the experience you want.

### Do all Iguazu tours include the Argentine side?

No. Visiting both countries requires time in the itinerary and an actual border crossing. Open the specific day-by-day program and check excursions, entrance tickets, and transfers.

### Is a long tour essential to experience Brazil's nature?

No. You can focus on one natural area. Long routes are best for travelers who want to compare several different biomes and are comfortable with transfers. A shorter trip often gives more time to appreciate a chosen place.

### Can Brazil be combined with Argentina and Peru?

Yes. For example, [Brazil and Argentina in 9 days](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-rio-iguazu-buenos-aires-9-days/) covers Rio, Iguazu, and Buenos Aires, while [Brazil, Argentina and Peru in 14 days](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-peru-14-days/) adds Cusco and Machu Picchu. The latter requires more time and consideration of altitude in the Andes.

## Lençóis Maranhenses in 4 days: lagoon season, dunes and the Preguiças River

This trip offers an introduction to [Lençóis Maranhenses National Park](/brazil/place/lencois-maranhenses/) without a multi-day hike across the entire area. Over **4 days and 3 nights**, the itinerary connects historic [São Luís](/brazil/place/sao-luis/), the excursion base of [Barreirinhas](/brazil/place/barreirinhas/), walks among white sand dunes, and a motorboat journey along the [Preguiças River](/brazil/place/preguicas-river/).

The main consideration when choosing dates is the seasonal condition of the lagoons. The white dunes remain throughout the year, but the blue pools between them fill with rainwater and gradually become shallower again. The same itinerary can therefore look completely different from one month to another.

## When should you travel to see the lagoons?

Lençóis Maranhenses lies on the coast of Maranhão state. Although the landscape resembles a sandy desert, it has a distinct rainy season, after which temporary freshwater lagoons appear between the dunes. In 2024, the area became a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

According to Brazil's conservation agency ICMBio, **May to September** is generally an especially favorable period for seeing full lagoons: rainfall in the preceding months leaves water between the sandy ridges, while the weather gradually becomes drier. Our itinerary describes the lagoon-forming season as March through September. These descriptions are not contradictory: the period when water appears and the most convenient period for seeing it are different.

The actual water level of [Lagoa Azul](/brazil/place/lagoa-azul-lencois-maranhenses/) depends on rainfall in a particular year. It is impossible to promise the same depth or color on every date. If swimming in lagoons is your main goal, choose the season around expected water levels; if you are interested in dunes, river scenery, and city history, the journey can still be worthwhile in other months.

## How the four days are arranged

| Day | Main stage |
|---|---|
| 1 | São Luís and hotel check-in |
| 2 | Barreirinhas, 4×4, lagoons |
| 3 | Preguiças River, stops, São Luís |
| 4 | Airport transfer |

The first day is spent in São Luís. Its historic center is known for tile-covered facades, cobbled streets, and colonial architecture. A separate [four-hour São Luís sightseeing excursion](/brazil/sao-luis/sao-luis-city-tour-4-hours/) is listed in the program as **optional** and must not automatically be counted as included in the base price.

On day two, after breakfast, travelers leave São Luís for Barreirinhas. The drive takes **approximately 4 hours**. After check-in and a rest, a 4×4 excursion heads into the dunes around Lagoa Azul, with an opportunity to swim and watch the sunset. This is the itinerary's principal sand-and-lagoon day.

Day three is devoted to a boat trip along the Preguiças River. The boat travels to [Vassouras](/brazil/place/vassouras-lencois-maranhenses/), an area known as Little Lençóis, then on toward a fishing village and the [Preguiças Lighthouse](/brazil/place/preguicas-lighthouse/). There are **160 steps** to its viewpoint. Following the river excursion, the group returns to São Luís. Day four concludes with the airport transfer.

## How the dune and river excursions differ

The lagoon outing takes place on sandy terrain. Short climbs over dunes, sun, wind, and the condition of the sand are important considerations. Authorized 4×4 vehicles transport visitors to some areas; vehicle access within the national park is governed by park management.

The Preguiças River presents a different scene. Vegetation along the banks, villages, sandy areas, and views toward the ocean coast alternate along the waterway. The lighthouse steps matter for travelers who prefer minimal physical exertion. Yet the river excursion does not replace walking among high white dunes: it is the combination of the two days that reveals the area's variety.

Both outings depend on weather and natural conditions. Sunscreen, a hat, drinking water, light covering clothing, and footwear suitable for sand are more practical than heavy city gear. A splashproof cover is helpful on the boat, while an extra light layer can be useful in the wind at sunset.

## Who should choose the short itinerary?

The four-day program works well if you want to see the main natural landscapes while reserving time for other parts of Brazil. It combines one city day and two different excursion days rather than a demanding trek across the entire park.

For travelers seeking more time in nature, compare [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/) and [journeys through the country's natural areas](/interests/wildlife/tours/brazil/). The main advantage here is the compact sequence São Luís → Barreirinhas → dunes and river → São Luís, with transfers already described.

## Frequently asked questions about Lençóis Maranhenses

### How long is the trip?

**4 days and 3 nights.** The main nature excursions take place on days two and three; days one and four are connected with arrival and departure from São Luís.

### When are the lagoons usually fullest?

Typically after the rainy season, approximately May to September. Actual water levels depend on rainfall each year, so choose swimming dates around expected lagoon conditions.

### Must I hike across the dunes for several days?

No. This itinerary includes a 4×4 excursion to the lagoons and a separate boat trip on the Preguiças River. A multi-day hike across the dunes is not listed.

### What matters most when choosing the itinerary?

The drive from São Luís to Barreirinhas, seasonal lagoon levels, sun exposure on the sand, and the steps to the lighthouse. A short program leaves less flexibility for weather changes, so choose dates according to your principal nature interest.

## A 16-day private tour of Brazil including the Amazon

This itinerary distributes **16 days and 15 nights** between Rio de Janeiro, the island coast, Iguazu Falls, the Amazon, and beaches near Porto de Galinhas. It is designed for travelers who want to combine active sightseeing with stays in specific hotels and several quiet days at the end.

The journey begins in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), includes a private boat trip toward [Ilha Grande](/brazil/place/ilha-grande/), and then continues to [Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). In the Amazon, guests stay not at a city hotel in Manaus but at a lodge near the [Anavilhanas archipelago](/brazil/place/anavilhanas-archipelago/). The final four full days are spent beside the ocean in the [Porto de Galinhas](/brazil/place/porto-de-galinhas/) area.

## Itinerary sequence and time to relax

| Days | Where the program takes place |
|---|---|
| 1–5 | Rio and a private boat to the islands |
| 6–7 | Iguazu and accommodation by the falls |
| 8–10 | Rio Negro and the Amazon |
| 11–15 | Porto de Galinhas and Muro Alto |
| 16 | Return via Rio |

**Rio, days 1–5.** After arrival, guests check in at Copacabana Palace. The itinerary continues to Sugarloaf Mountain, the historic center, Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer, and a private boat trip toward the islands. In the New Year's version of the program, a separate evening is dedicated to celebrating New Year's Eve on Copacabana. When choosing dates, it is therefore essential to match the actual arrival date to this festive stage rather than assuming it is available on any day of the year.

**Iguazu, days 6–7.** After a flight, guests stay at Belmond Hotel das Cataratas inside the national park. The itinerary includes a walk on the Brazilian side of the falls. Other experiences, including Macuco Safari, should be distinguished from the paid main excursion.

**Amazon, days 8–10.** Via Manaus, travelers reach Mirante do Gavião Amazon Lodge near Novo Airão. The program includes boat outings, an introduction to the Rio Negro's nature, and a trip into Anavilhanas National Park. One day features visits to the communities of [Santo Antônio](/brazil/place/santo-antonio-amazon/) and [Tiririca](/brazil/place/tiririca-amazon/), relaxing by the river, and wildlife watching. Dolphin encounters are described as a possibility in their natural habitat, **not guaranteed appearances on a schedule**.

**Ocean, days 11–15.** After a flight to [Recife](/brazil/place/recife/) and a transfer to the coast, guests check in at Nannai Muro Alto. The following four days have no compulsory excursions, leaving time for the beach and relaxation after the flights, waterfalls, and boat trips.

## What distinguishes the hotels on this itinerary?

The program specifies a particular range of accommodation, which matters when assessing its cost and pace:

- **Copacabana Palace**, Rio: 4 nights, One Bedroom Double Suite with a pool view and breakfast.
- **Belmond Hotel das Cataratas**, Iguazu: Deluxe room with breakfast at the hotel inside the national park.
- **Mirante do Gavião Amazon Lodge**, Amazon: Deluxe room, full board, a pier on the Rio Negro, and Camu Camu restaurant.
- **Nannai Muro Alto**, coast: double bungalow with an ocean view and half board.

All these stops are part of the itinerary. If necessary, we may substitute another hotel of the same category. When confirming arrangements, therefore check not only the star rating but also the location, room type, meals, and proximity to major attractions.

## The Amazon beyond Manaus

[Anavilhanas](/brazil/place/anavilhanas-archipelago/) is a system of islands and channels on the Rio Negro, where a boat excursion is very different from a city sightseeing tour. The itinerary includes a boat, visits to small communities, and a lodge stay outside Manaus. Getting to this region requires time for ground transfers and boat logistics.

Some activities are **optional extras**, including seaplane flights and particular ways of observing dolphins. They must not automatically be treated as paid for just because they are described alongside the main itinerary days.

The journey deliberately does not end with an international flight immediately after the Amazon. The beach section at Muro Alto means the last days are not spent constantly moving between airports.

## Price, guiding and flights

The price of this journey is **$30,633**; when comparing it with other tours, consider the actual accommodation conditions and included services. Included are hotel stays with the stated meal arrangements, excursions, transfers with a driver, and entrance tickets.

Guiding varies by region: a Russian-speaking guide is provided in Rio, while English-speaking guides lead excursions in the Amazon and several other parts of the route. It would be inaccurate to describe the entire 16-day itinerary as exclusively Russian-guided.

**Domestic flights are not included.** The program gives an indicative domestic airfare **from $1,050 per person**. Additional excursions, food, and drinks beyond those specified in the itinerary are paid for separately. This is an important part of budgeting for an extended journey.

## Who is the 16-day program for?

This trip suits guests interested in several climatic and natural regions within one holiday. It combines city sightseeing, a private sea outing, waterfalls, tropical forest, and several days at the ocean. The intensive first half requires readiness for domestic flights, but the final stage stays within one beach area.

If you do not need the Amazon and a long beach finale, consider a [week-long Rio tour](/brazil/tour/best-of-rio-de-janeiro/). For Rio, both sides of Iguazu, and Búzios, there is a [9-day itinerary](/brazil/tour/best-of-brazil-9-days/). Browse all the options in [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about the private tour including the Amazon

### How long is the Amazon section?

Days 8–10 are devoted to the Amazon: the lodge stay, river excursions, and return via Manaus.

### Where does the beach holiday take place?

At Muro Alto near Porto de Galinhas, with accommodation at Nannai Muro Alto. Four days here are free from compulsory excursions.

### Is New Year's Eve on Copacabana part of the itinerary?

Yes. The New Year's version includes a separate festive evening in Rio. Actual arrival dates must coincide with this event.

### Are guides Russian-speaking throughout the tour?

No. In several regions, including the Amazon and Recife, travelers are accompanied by English-speaking guides.

### Are domestic airline tickets included in the price?

No. They are paid for separately; the itinerary gives an indicative price from $1,050 per person.

## Premium Rio Carnival and Iguazu: an 8-day itinerary

This trip is defined as much by its travel format as by Carnival itself. In Rio, it includes accommodation at **Copacabana Palace**, private excursions with a Russian-speaking guide, a Carnival evening, a 30-minute flight above the city, and travel by deluxe minivan. The second part takes place at **Belmond Hotel das Cataratas** by [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), including walks on both sides and a private Macuco Safari boat.

The duration is **8 days and 7 nights**: 5 nights in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and 2 at Iguazu. The main difference from a simpler Carnival tour is the specific services, hotels' locations, and guiding format.

## Accommodation and main experiences

| Stage | What the itinerary includes |
|---|---|
| Rio | Copacabana Palace, excursions, Carnival |
| Above the city | 30-minute helicopter flight |
| Sambadrome | Carnival tickets, Frisa box |
| Iguazu | Belmond, both sides of the falls |
| On the river | Private Macuco Safari boat |

In Rio, accommodation is in a **Deluxe Ocean View Room** at Copacabana Palace with breakfast. Visitors ascend Corcovado through Tijuca Forest to Christ the Redeemer, then explore the historic center. Sugarloaf Mountain offers another view of the bay and beaches; VIP Access / Fast Track for the day-four ascent is listed among the included services.

The program also includes **the Carnival Ball at Copacabana Palace**. Because the list of included services describes tickets under the general term “Carnival tickets,” the actual ticket arrangements for the ball itself should be reconciled with the confirmed offer. Mentioning the event in the itinerary does not determine the category of every ticket.

Another Rio highlight is a **30-minute helicopter excursion**, included in the price. At the Sambadrome, the plan specifies a separate **Frisa box, sector 4, row A/B, with 6 seats**, with a private transfer and guide. These details distinguish the product from a standard group seat in the stands.

At Iguazu, accommodation is in a **Junior Suite** at Belmond Hotel das Cataratas with breakfast. The hotel is inside the national park. The Brazilian-side walk offers panoramic views of the cascades, while the private Macuco Safari boat takes guests closer to the water. On the Argentine side, the itinerary follows walkways and an ecological train toward Devil's Throat.

## Important: Carnival and Champions' Parade dates

## Luxury Rio Carnival, Iguazu and Alagoas: how the 11-day trip works

This itinerary includes **5 nights in Rio de Janeiro**, **2 nights near Iguazu**, and **3 nights on the Alagoas coast**. The main idea is to spend Carnival nights in the city, view the waterfalls from different sides, and end with a restful oceanfront stay. The sequence makes sense after late returns from festive events: the most intensive stage is at the beginning, with free days saved for the end.

[Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) is the setting for Carnival, Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain, and a helicopter flight. [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) becomes the base for visiting the falls, while [Alagoas](/brazil/place/alagoas/) is the final beach stage. Although an excursion to the [Argentine side of Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) is mandatory within the itinerary, Brazil remains the tour's main destination.

## Carnival nights: the ball and Sambadrome are different events

On day one, guests arrive in Rio, receive a private transfer with Russian-speaking assistance, and check in at **Belmond Copacabana Palace**, in a Deluxe Ocean View room with breakfast. The evening is free. Airport Fast Track can be booked for an additional charge; it is not part of the basic package.

Day two includes Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer, along with an introduction to the historic center. The evening features **the Carnival Ball at Copacabana Palace**. The ball starts at 22:00 and continues until approximately 05:00, so the following morning is deliberately kept free.

Day three features a **30-minute helicopter flight over Rio**, followed in the evening by the main Carnival show at the Sambadrome. A separate **Frisa box, sector 4, row A/B**, with room for 6 guests is specified. The itinerary includes private transport and a guide; guests are not obliged to remain until the end of all overnight performances.

**The hotel ball and the samba school parade at the Sambadrome are not the same event.** These are two evenings with different forms of participation and dress. After the Sambadrome night, day four again has a free morning, followed by an ascent of Sugarloaf Mountain with included VIP Fast Track access to the cable car.

Official parade dates are set annually by LIESA. When selecting a departure, match **the specific year**, parade days, ball program, and tickets in the selected sector. February dates from one Carnival season cannot automatically be applied to another.

## Iguazu: two countries and several ways to experience the falls

On day six, travelers fly from Rio to Foz do Iguaçu and check in at **Belmond das Cataratas**, in a Junior Suite with breakfast. The hotel is inside the national park. That day includes panoramic viewing from the Brazilian side of the falls, a private **Macuco Safari** boat, a 10-minute helicopter flight, and the Bird Park. All these items are listed among this particular tour's inclusions.

Day seven is an excursion to [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) in Argentina. A Russian-speaking guide, the ecological train, and walking routes allow guests to approach the waterfalls from the other side, including Devil's Throat. Documents allowing travelers to cross the international border and return to Brazil must be arranged in advance.

Cross-border visits to Iguazu involve separate logistics and entry requirements depending on nationality. We help fit this excursion into the route, but its inclusion does not exempt anyone from border formalities. Check the conditions for your passport and travel date.

## Three nights by the ocean after Carnival

On day eight, the itinerary calls for a flight to [Maceió](/brazil/place/maceio/) via Rio and a private onward transfer to **Kenoa Exclusive Beach Spa & Resort**. Accommodation is in an **Apoena Suite of 45 m²**, with a terrace and a coastal view. Breakfast is included.

Days nine and ten are free. You can spend them at the beach, relax at the hotel, and choose restaurants independently. This finale differs significantly from an itinerary with excursions every day. Day eleven includes a transfer to Maceió Airport and a return journey via Rio or São Paulo for an international flight.
